podcast.body: A toned-down, sanitized cover version of Little Richard's song, released a year after the original. This version allowed the song to be played in mainstream (white) places, including white radio stations, and helped cover the rest of the marketplace. "Having Pat Boone record 2D Fruity that way, allowed the song to be played in more places, including all those hard to get white radio stations."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Pat Boone released an "inept white cover version" of Little Richard's hit "Tutti Frutti." Boone changed some lyrics, notably altering Richard's interest in both Sue and Daisy to reflect his "good Christian boy" image, and made other minor word changes to create full sentences. "Now, notice that there Boone changes the lyrics."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.body: Pat Boone's "watered down" version of "Tutti Frutti," which debuted just a couple of weeks after Little Richard's original. Boone's rendition peaked at number 12 on the pop charts. "Pat Hoon debuted with his Water Down version. The Boon rendition of 2D Frudey peaked at number 12 on the pop charts"
